# Independent audit of the width-two sharp simplex product

Audited the complete exact certificate in
`candidate ec1a047aab7b654b`
and reran `supporting computation verify_width_two_sharp_product_unique_heavy_plane.py`
with plain Python. **PASS; no correction needed.** The verifier
returns the displayed 29 facets, 16 exposure gaps, and all 29
nonzero rank witnesses for the other parity classes.

The cofactor enumeration covers every facet. A facet of this
full-dimensional four-polytope contains four affinely independent
vertices; their three difference vectors have a nonzero cofactor
normal. The one-sided test keeps exactly supporting such planes.
Conversely every kept plane contains a three-dimensional vertex
simplex, hence is a facet. Its orientation and primitive reduction
are correct. The bounding-box enumeration therefore checks the
whole hull, not a merely outer polyhedral approximation, and finds
exactly the sixteen listed integer points among the 432 possibilities.

At each point the sum of active outward normals strictly exposes
that point: every individual facet contribution to an exposure gap
is nonnegative, and the exact resulting minimum gaps are positive.
Thus all sixteen points really are vertices. They have distinct
parities and exhaust the parity classes.

The all-hyperplane test is stronger than the facet enumeration and
is independently sound. The affine span of any lattice points in
any real hyperplane is rational and proper. It lies in a primitive
integer hyperplane, whose mod-two normal is nonzero. Hence at most
eight of the sixteen parity-distinct points can lie in the original
hyperplane. Eight points would comprise an entire affine mod-two
hyperplane class. All thirty such classes are checked: twenty-nine
have full affine rank four, while the remaining class has rank
three and lies in z1=1. This proves uniqueness of that actual
hyperplane. The points at z1=0 and z1=2 show it is internal.
Supporting hyperplanes thus have at most seven points; the exact
facet counts also show that seven is attained.

The width argument checks both directions. The first coordinate
has width two. If a nonzero integer functional had width one on
the seed e1,e2,e3,e4,(2,2,3,5), its coefficients would be t or
t+1. Its value at the fifth point implies

    11t + 2 epsilon1 + 2 epsilon2 + 3 epsilon3
        + 5 epsilon4 belongs to {0,1}.

Only t=0 or t=-1 is possible. The missing subset sums one and
eleven force, respectively, all epsilons zero or all one, both
giving the zero functional. Full dimension excludes nonzero
width-zero functionals. Therefore the lattice width is exactly two.

For the product with any positive d-simplex, the actual integer
fibers are exactly the sixteen simplex copies. Its full convex
hull is exactly the original product body. The own-fiber centroid
bound holds for every ambient containing cap, including zero
continuous normal. Conversely the displayed exposed-base caps
strictly exclude every other fiber: the integer exposure gap is
at least one, whereas a barycentric coordinate is at most one.
On the own fiber they are precisely canonical simplex caps, of
fraction Gamma_d. Their finite cover proves the global upper
bound at every candidate point. The exact maximal depth is thus
Gamma_d/16, with no restriction on oblique integer tilts.

The limitation is exactly a supporting-base-hyperplane limitation.
The source has an internal affine hyperplane of mass one half,
and every supporting base hyperplane has mass at most seven
sixteenths. It is not an example with all affine hyperplanes
strictly below one half. The separate conditional estimate in
Section 4 correctly obtains Gamma_d(1-eta)/(N-k) from a heaviest
fiber outside an actual k-point hyperplane; it does not establish
the needed half-cardinality incidence for arbitrary empty
polytopes. The optional classical low-dimensional width statement
is not used in any of the exact certificate or depth calculations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
